metric: Pairs shown different by a constraint-respecting database on which both queries were run (DuckDB), and pairs on which 600 random databases (400 wider ones when a query has HAVING, and every database of at most 2 rows per table) showed no difference (not a proof, not bounded verification).
correctness: Every refutation was executed on both queries, is stable under row-order shuffles, and returns the same rows with DuckDB's optimizer off; none are claimed without a database
coverage_of: The 19,201 pairs the prover leaves unknown in verieql-leetcode-proof (the other 4,793 of 23,994 are proved there): refuted, unknown (agree on every database tried) or unsupported (not run).
caveats: Full corpus (23,994 pairs). No labels. MySQL source run on DuckDB; 1,071 pairs are not run (DuckDB rejects them, mostly a table name the schema spells differently and GROUP BY positions that name aggregates). Search settings were tuned on a 1,000-pair sample (every 24th pair), so the other pairs are held out from that tuning. Measured on master 7b7ba13 (harness translation #347, HAVING-only wider search #356); prover rules merged later (cast_rules.py and after) are not rerun yet. In this row 'unknown' counts pairs that agree on every database tried and 'unsupported' counts pairs DuckDB or the parser rejects. VeriEQL marks 30 of these refutations equivalent; those read by hand differ on an empty table or a NULL that VeriEQL's bounded search did not reach.
held_out: Search settings tuned on every 24th pair (1,000); the other 22,994 pairs are unseen. 3,310 of the 3,586 pairs VeriEQL refutes are refuted here too (92%).
